title: Thank You!
subtitle: Four ways to say thank you
review: Text and notes written by Claude: check them. No Burmese yet. The baker and the man have no voice of their own yet: add them to "voice" before recording by scene.
intro: A birthday present that looks familiar, two croissants for a woman on a diet, a compliment about the wrong dinner and directions to a train that leaves in two minutes: four short scenes. Listen for how people say thank you, and how they answer.

lines.text: Happy birthday, Emma! This is for you.
lines.note: This is for you: say it when you give a present.

lines.text: Oh, you shouldn't have!
lines.note: You shouldn't have! = you are too kind. A polite thing to say when you get a present.

lines.text: Open it!
A scarf! It's beautiful. Thank you so much!
lines.note: Thank you so much: stronger than Thank you.

lines.text: You're welcome. Blue is your color.
lines.note: You're welcome: the usual answer to Thank you. Color (American) = colour (British).

lines.text: I know. I lost this scarf in March.
lines.note: Lost: past of lose. She lost the scarf, and now it is a present.

lines.text: And I found it. Don't mention it.
lines.note: Don't mention it = you're welcome. Here it also means: please do not talk about it!

lines.text: Good morning! What can I get you?
lines.note: What can I get you? = What would you like?

lines.text: A baguette and two croissants, please.
lines.note: Please: always add it when you ask for something.

lines.text: Here you go. Anything else?
lines.note: Here you go: say it when you give something to a person. Anything else? = Do you want more?

lines.text: No, thank you. I'm on a diet.
lines.note: No, thank you: the polite way to say no. On a diet: eating less to lose weight.

lines.text: With two croissants?
They're for Lucas. Both of them. Officially.
lines.note: Officially: this is what she tells people. It may not be true.

lines.text: Of course. That's four fifty.
lines.note: Four fifty = four dollars and fifty cents.

lines.text: Here you go. Thanks a lot!
lines.note: Thanks a lot! Informal and friendly.

lines.text: My pleasure. Say hi to Lucas.
lines.note: My pleasure = you're welcome: I was happy to do it. Say hi to… = give my greeting to…

lines.text: It's late. I should get going.
lines.note: I should get going = I should leave now.

lines.text: Already? One more coffee?
lines.note: Already? = so soon?

lines.text: No, thank you. I'm fine, thanks.
lines.note: I'm fine, thanks = I do not need anything.

lines.text: Thank you for coming!
lines.note: Thank you for coming: thank you for + verb-ing.

lines.text: Thanks for everything. The fish was delicious.
lines.note: Thanks for everything: thanks for + noun.

lines.text: It was chicken.
… Thanks again. Good night!
lines.note: Thanks again: say it at the end, when you have already said thank you.

lines.text: Excuse me, sir. I'm looking for the train station.
lines.note: Excuse me: say it first when you stop a stranger. Sir: polite, to a man.

lines.text: The station? Go straight, then turn left.
lines.note: Go straight: do not turn.

lines.text: Straight, then left. Is it far?
No. Five minutes on foot.
lines.note: On foot = walking.

lines.text: Thanks for your help. You're a lifesaver!
lines.note: Thanks for your help. You're a lifesaver! = you helped me very much. Informal.

lines.text: Anytime. What time is your train?
lines.note: Anytime = you're welcome; I will help again.

lines.text: In two minutes.
Then thank me later. Run!
lines.note: Thank me later = no time for thanks now.

notes: Thank you is for everyone. Thanks and Thanks a lot are friendly. Thank you so much is stronger.
Thanks for + noun or verb-ing: Thanks for your help. Thank you for coming.
To answer: You're welcome. My pleasure. Anytime. Don't mention it.
No, thank you says no politely. I'm fine, thanks means you do not need anything.
When you get a present: You shouldn't have! It means you are very kind.
Thanks again comes at the end, when you have already said thank you.

questions.q: A friend gives you a present. Which is a polite thing to say?
questions.why: You shouldn't have! = this is too kind. It is a way of saying thank you.

questions.q: “Anything else?” You do not want more. What do you say?
questions.why: No, thank you is the polite way to say no.

questions.q: Somebody says “Thanks for your help.” What can you answer?
questions.why: Anytime = you're welcome; I am happy to help again.

questions.q: Lucas says “Don't mention it.” What does this usually mean?
questions.why: Don't mention it is a polite answer to thank you. In the scene it is also a joke: he does not want to talk about the scarf.
